candidates.source_description: The Flammenwerfer became one of the most feared weapons of World War I, first seeing major German use in 1915. Designed primarily for clearing enemy trenches and fortified positions, it projected a stream of burning fuel over short distances and could force defenders from protected positions. Its psychological impact was often greater than its tactical range, creating panic and making it particularly effective during assaults on fortified areas. candidates.source_description:
In the early 1900s, desperate parents brought their premature babies to one of the strangest places imaginable: a Coney Island amusement park.

At the time, many hospitals lacked adequate facilities for premature infants, and their chances of survival were frighteningly low. Martin Couney began caring for these babies inside specially designed incubators—but he funded their treatment in an unusual way.
